extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Living and non-living (chemistry focus) — matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Both living and non-living things are made of matter. (2) Solids — have a fixed shape and fixed volume. Particles are packed tightly. Examples: stone, brick, ice, pencil, book, wood, metal. (3) Liquids — have a fixed volume but take the shape of their container. Particles are close but can move. Examples: water, milk, oil, juice, honey. (4) Gases — have no fixed shape and no fixed volume. They spread to fill any container. Particles are far apart and move freely. Examples: air, steam, oxygen, smoke, helium. (5) Properties of solids, liquids, gases — solids: fixed shape + fixed volume, hard to compress. Liquids: takes container shape + fixed volume, flows, hard to compress. Gases: no fixed shape + no fixed volume, spreads everywhere, easy to compress. State changes: melting (solid→liquid), evaporation (liquid→gas), condensation (gas→liquid), freezing (liquid→solid). Water can be all three: ice (solid), water (liquid), steam (gas). Misconceptions: 'air is nothing' (air is a gas — it has mass and takes up space), 'liquids have no shape' (liquids have the shape of their container — they do have a shape, just not a fixed one), 'ice and water are different substances' (ice is frozen water — same substance in different states), 'gas has no weight' (gas has weight — a balloon full of air weighs more than an empty one). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function MatterGame), NOT export default. Export interface MatterGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void.
